MATH.description: Mathematics (4024) is the toolkit you'll use in almost every other subject and all through life — from handling money and measurements to reading charts and solving problems. Across the two years you'll strengthen your number sense, work with algebra and graphs, study shape, space and measurement, get to grips with trigonometry, and learn to make sense of data and chance. The course is built from the nine topics below, and your final papers can test any of them.

topics.name: Mensuration
subtopics: Compound shapes and parts of shapes

PHY.description: Physics (5054) explains how the world works, from everyday motion and energy to electricity, waves, the atom and outer space. You'll learn to describe things with measurements and formulas, carry out and interpret experiments, and connect ideas across the six topics below. It builds the reasoning and practical skills that underpin engineering, medicine and the sciences.

topics.name: Nuclear physics
subtopics: The nuclear model of the atom

CHEM.description: Chemistry (5070) is the study of what everything is made of and how substances change. You'll explore atoms and bonding, chemical reactions and energy, acids and salts, the Periodic Table, metals, the environment and organic chemistry, and learn the laboratory techniques chemists use to make and identify substances. It's the foundation for medicine, materials, and understanding the world around you.

topics.name: Atoms, elements and compounds
subtopics: Atomic structure and the Periodic Table

topics.name: Stoichiometry
subtopics: Relative masses of atoms and molecules
The mole and the Avogadro constant

topics.name: Acids, bases and salts
subtopics: The characteristic properties of acids and bases

CS.description: Computer Science (2210) teaches how computers really work and how to solve problems with them. One half covers computer systems — how data is represented and moved, hardware and software, the internet, security and new technologies. The other half is algorithms, programming and logic — designing solutions, writing and testing programs, databases and Boolean logic. It builds genuine problem-solving and coding skills.

topics.name: Data transmission
subtopics: Types and methods of data transmission

topics.name: Software
subtopics: Types of programming language, translators and integrated development environments (IDEs)

topics.name: The internet and its uses
subtopics: The internet and the world wide web

ECON.description: Economics (2281) is about how people, businesses and governments make choices when resources are limited. You'll learn how markets set prices, how firms and workers behave, how governments manage the economy, and how countries trade and develop. It gives you a sharp lens on the news, money and the decisions that shape everyday life.

topics.name: The basic economic problem
subtopics: The nature of the basic economic problem

topics.name: The allocation of resources
subtopics: The role of markets in allocating resources

topics.name: Economic development
subtopics: Differences in economic development between countries

topics.name: International trade and globalisation
subtopics: Current account of the balance of payments

BUS.description: Business (7081) shows how organisations are set up and run, and why some succeed. You'll look at how businesses start and grow, how they manage people, market their products, produce goods and services, handle money, and respond to the wider world around them. It's practical, real-world knowledge for anyone curious about enterprise, management or working life.

topics.name: Operations management
subtopics: Technology and production of goods and services
Sustainable production of goods and services
Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis

ACC.description: Accounting (7707) is the language of business — how money coming in and going out is recorded, checked and turned into a clear picture of how an organisation is doing. You'll learn double-entry book-keeping, how to prepare and verify financial statements, and how to read them to judge performance. It's a precise, practical skill valued in almost every career.

topics.name: Sources and recording of data
subtopics: The double entry system of book-keeping

topics.name: Accounting procedures
subtopics: Capital and revenue expenditure and receipts
Accounting for depreciation and disposal of non-current assets
Irrecoverable debts and allowance for irrecoverable debts

topics.name: Analysis and interpretation
subtopics: Calculation and understanding of accounting ratios

ISL.description: Islamiyat (2058) is a careful study of the foundations of Islam — the Qur'an and its major themes, the life and importance of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), the Hadiths, the Rightly Guided Caliphs, and the core beliefs and pillars of the faith. You'll learn to give accounts of key events and teachings and to explain their meaning for Muslims today.

topics.name: Major themes of the Qur'an
subtopics: God's relationship with the created world

topics.name: The history and importance of the Qur'an
subtopics: Revelation and compilation of the Qur'an
The Qur'an as the basis of thought and action in Islam

topics.name: The life and importance of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)
subtopics: From birth to the call to prophethood

topics.name: Major teachings in the Hadiths of the Prophet
The history and importance of the Hadiths
subtopics: The main collections and their significance

topics.name: The period of rule of the Rightly Guided Caliphs
subtopics: Main events of the four Caliphs' rules
Their significance as examples of leadership

topics.name: The Articles of Faith and the Pillars of Islam
subtopics: Jihad in its range of meanings

PST1.description: History of Pakistan (Paper 1 of Pakistan Studies 2059) traces how Pakistan came to be and how it grew as a nation. You'll study the cultural and historical roots of the Pakistan Movement, the events that led to independence in 1947, and the country's journey as a nation since. It builds skills in using historical sources and explaining causes and consequences.

topics.name: Cultural and historical background to the Pakistan Movement

PST2.description: Environment of Pakistan (Paper 2 of Pakistan Studies 2059) is the geography of the country — its land, resources and the challenges of developing them sustainably. You'll study the landscape and climate, natural resources and power, farming, industry, trade, transport and the population. It develops skills in reading maps, data and environmental sources.

topics.name: Natural resources - an issue of sustainability

ENG.description: English Language (1123) builds the reading and writing you'll rely on in every subject and beyond. You'll learn to understand what texts say and imply, to summarise and select information, and to write clearly and correctly for different purposes and audiences. The course is assessed in two papers: Reading and Writing.

URDU.description: Urdu Language (3248) develops confident reading and writing in Urdu. You'll practise understanding and responding to texts, writing clearly for different purposes, and using grammar and translation accurately. The course is assessed in two papers: Reading and Writing, and Grammar, Writing and Translation.
